newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-UNLIKELY CONTENDERS COULD CLINCH NATIONS CUP BERTH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNLIKELY CONTENDERS COULD CLINCH NATIONS CUP BERTH.

text.p: Malawi, Namibia and Togo head the list of unlikely contenders who can clinch a berth in next year's African Nations Cup finals by winning qualifying matches this weekend.

Malawi need just a draw away against neighbours Zambia to qualify for the finals in Burkina Faso next February for only the second time while a home victory for Togo against Liberia could see them through for the first time in 14 years.
Namibia can qualify for their first-ever Nations Cup finals appearance if they beat Cameroon in Windhoek on Saturday, a feat which would have seemed possible about six months ago.

The Namibiams, who were on the receiving end of a 7-1 hiding by Egypt last November, have since burst through the African footballing ranks to head the standings in group five and start as favourites for the match against Cameroon, whose Belgian coach HenriDepireux resigned last week.

The home team will be without key defender Mohamed Ouseb, who is suspended after receiving a second red card in the qualifiers, and German-bound winger Eliphas Shivute, who has gone back to Europe for pre-season training.
But Namibia will have teenager striker Razundura Tjikuzu back from Werder Bremen for his first appearance in seven games.
Depireux stormed out of Cameroon earlier this month saying he was not receiving any co-operation from footballing authorities and has been replaced by a five-man locally-based coaching committee.

Malawi are top of group seven and need just a point from their last two matches. But both games are away, starting with Zambia in Lusaka on Saturday, and might just be beyond the reach of Ruben Malola's team.

A win for Zambia would also put them through but coach George Mungwa has been struggling to assemble his squad on the eve of the match. The silver-haired trainer gave five foreign-based professional an ultimatum on Wednesday to report to the training amp or be left out of the squad, including captain Jonson Bwalya.

Togo will again be relying on German-based Bachirou Salou for their goals against a Liberian team led by George Weah. Sunday's game in group six is Liberia's last chance to stay in the qualification race while three points for the hosts will see them into the Nations Cup finals for the third time in 22 tournaments.
Other countries who can secure qalification this weekend are either Ghana or Zimbabwe in group one; Mali, the Ivory Coast, Morocco, Senegal and Guinea.

The winner of the match between Ghana and Zimbabwe in Kumasi will settle top place in group one and Guinea can secure a qualifying place from group four if they draw or win away against Tunisia on Saturday.
